conventions: stop entries mechanized as signal-bar-close then next-bar-open; every tunable constant is a parameter; long side only in pseudocode, sides field says mirrored/same. Helpers: gapSize(n) = max(0, low[n]-high[n+1]) for a bull gap / max(0, low[n+1]-high[n]) for a bear gap (0 when the bars overlap); averageDailyRange(N) = average of (high-low) over the N bars ending at bar 1.

candidates.name: GapOpeningDefinition
candidates.quote: A gap opening on any time frame means that once the bar in question closes, it does not overlap the bar before it.
candidates.description: Shared primitive: the current bar's range does not overlap the prior bar's range -- a gap up (this bar's low above the prior bar's high) or gap down (this bar's high below the prior bar's low).
candidates.book_order_type: n/a (bar classification, treated like any other breakout for order placement)

complexity.reason: single fixed-offset comparison between two bars' ranges; identical whether the bar is intraday or daily -- Brooks states this explicitly ('on any time frame') and separately notes daily-chart gaps trade the same way as 5-minute gaps

notes: Brooks: 'It does not matter whether there is also a gap on the daily chart, since the trading will be the same' -- confirms this same test is meant to run on daily bars.

candidates.name: LargeGapByRecentMax
candidates.quote: As another guideline, if the gap is the largest gap of the past five days or so ... it can be considered to be a large gap.
candidates.description: The current bar's gap (V20-01) is at least as large as the largest gap seen over the prior N bars -- one of two alternative 'large gap' tests.
candidates.book_order_type: n/a (bar classification feeding a trend-day expectation)

complexity.reason: a windowed highest() over a derived per-bar gap-size series

notes: Brooks gives this as a rough guideline ('or so'), not a strict rule; kept as a separate candidate from V20-03 because the book offers them as alternative ('or') tests.

candidates.name: LargeGapByAvgRangeFraction
candidates.quote: ... or if it is larger than about half of the average daily range, it can be considered to be a large gap.
candidates.description: The current bar's gap (V20-01) exceeds a fraction of the recent average bar range -- the second of the two alternative 'large gap' tests.
candidates.book_order_type: n/a (bar classification feeding a trend-day expectation)

complexity.reason: a windowed average of (high-low) compared against the derived gap size

notes: rangeLookback of 20 is a reading of 'average daily range' with no bar count given; Brooks separately uses 20-bar EMAs elsewhere in the trilogy, used here for consistency.

candidates.name: TradeWithGapDirectionBias
candidates.quote: The larger a gap is, the more likely it will be the start of a trend day away from yesterday's close ... Whenever you see a large gap opening, it is wise to assume that there will be a strong trend.
candidates.description: Context filter: on a large-gap day (V20-02 or V20-03), bias entries for the rest of the session toward the gap's direction (long after a large gap up, short after a large gap down), favoring with-trend setups (trend-from-open, breakout pullback) over countertrend ones.
candidates.pseudocode: (low[0] - high[1]) >= largeGapTicks * tick /* placeholder for V20-02 or V20-03 */ && direction == up
candidates.book_order_type: n/a (directional bias filter, not itself an order)

complexity.reason: the underlying gap-size test is simple, but 'bias toward the gap direction' is a qualitative preference among later setups rather than a single decidable test, and Brooks's own probabilities (50/20/30) are explicitly guidelines, not fixed thresholds

notes: Brooks gives illustrative probabilities (e.g. large gap up: ~50% bull channel, ~20% trading range, ~30% bear trend) that he explicitly says are not precise; not encoded as literals.

candidates.name: BigGapUnclearActionRangeAssumption
candidates.quote: If there is a big gap but the price action is unclear, assume that the market is forming a trading range and look to buy low and sell high.
candidates.description: Context filter: on a large-gap day where the opening bars do not show clear trend behavior, default to a range assumption and favor mean-reversion (buy near the range low, sell near the range high) instead of breakout entries.
candidates.book_order_type: n/a (context filter selecting a trading mode)

complexity.reason: 'price action is unclear' has no bar-level definition in the text; a design decision is needed for what counts as a clear trend versus unclear action before this can be coded

notes: hasTrendBarSequence is a placeholder for whatever 'clear trend' primitive the authoring pass settles on; kept research grade deliberately.

candidates.name: GapAsSpikeForChannelTrend
candidates.quote: The gap should be looked at as if it is one huge, invisible trend bar. For example, if there is a large gap up and it is followed by a minor pullback and then a channel type of rally for the rest of the day, this is likely a gap spike and channel bull trend, with the gap being the spike.
candidates.description: Treat a large gap as the 'spike' leg of a spike-and-channel trend: if a minor pullback is followed by a channel-type continuation in the gap's direction, classify the day as a gap spike-and-channel trend in that direction.

complexity.reason: requires pivot/pullback detection and channel-line projection over a variable-length window following the gap, on top of the gap test itself

notes: 'Spike and channel' is expected to be a shared primitive defined in another chapter (e.g. the trends volume or the reversals climax chapters); this candidate is the gap-specific instance of it.

rejected.quote: For example, a large gap up has perhaps a 50 percent chance of being followed by a bull channel, a 20 percent chance of being followed by a trading range, and a 30 percent chance of being followed by a bear trend. These probabilities are only guidelines...
rejected.reason: Brooks explicitly disclaims these as inexact guidelines, not a stated threshold or rule; no bar-level test to encode

rejected.quote: TradeStation Chart Analysis - $INDU 5 min [US] Dow Jones Industrial Average ... Bar 1 was bull trend bar on a large gap up day. The day became a trend from the open, gap spike and channel bull trend.

rejected.quote: traders who bought during those first several bars were risking about 10 points to make about 15 to 20 points, and they had a 60 percent chance of success, which is a great trade.

chapter_summary: Defines a gap opening as non-overlap between the current bar and the prior bar's range -- explicitly stated to work identically on any time frame including the daily chart -- and gives two alternative 'large gap' thresholds (largest of the last ~5 bars, or beyond about half the average range). The rest of the chapter is a probabilistic argument that large gaps raise the odds of a trend day and should be traded like other breakouts (trend-from-open, failed breakout, breakout pullback -- concepts expected from other chapters), plus a fallback range-trading assumption when the post-gap price action is unclear. GapOpeningDefinition (V20-01) and the two large-gap tests (V20-02, V20-03) are the load-bearing, cleanly mechanizable candidates and are explicitly daily-bar compatible; the trend-day bias and channel-classification candidates (V20-04..V20-06) are softer, research/hard-grade filters.
